- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.6) and forecast is significantly below recent highs, adjust upward by 1–2% to account for momentum.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and forecast is above recent lows, reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overcorrection.
- If forecast spikes sharply after a recent low, apply a 10–15% downward correction to prevent overshoot.
- If forecast mean reverts too quickly after a spike, delay correction by 1–2 periods to match sentiment lag.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently 2–3% below forecast, reduce forecast by 1–2% in next period to align with mean reversion.
- If sentiment history shows repeated bullish sentiment but forecast remains flat or declining, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to reflect sentiment bias.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.3–0.6) and forecast is volatile, smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 values to reduce noise.
